claims.statement: For the standard complexified real 16-dimensional Spin(9) spinor and the ordinary tensor representation S* tensor S tensor S, an independent exact 12-qubit Pauli-word/Casimir-projector calculation recovers the five isotypic dimensions (16,128,432,768,672) with multiplicities (5,4,3,2,1), resolves both output-swap sectors with dimensions 2176 and 1920, and certifies the support-gap star blocks are PSD at all ten exact mixed-weight cone rays, conditional on the supplied canonical-EB support vertices (1,0,0,14), (0,1,7,7), (1,4,4,6).
assumptions: Spin(9) acts in its standard real 16-dimensional spinor representation, complexified to M_16.
The Clifford grade basis is T_A=i^(k(k-1)/2) Gamma_A for grades 0 through 4, with tau=Tr/16.
The three-vertex canonical-EB support formula is supplied by the separate pure-spinor orbit task; this audit does not prove it.
The covariant dual reduction and comparison inequality are supplied by the main theorem argument; this audit covers only the ordinary tensor star block component.
claims.status: internal exact independent hostile audit; not proof-assistant verified; conditional block certificate
costs: The exact sparse word replay covers dimension 4096 and 90 nonempty representation/output-swap blocks across ten rays.
Casimir powers through degree five have Pauli support sizes 1, 109, 2755, 18127, 32896, and 32896; star-gap powers are recorded per ray in the JSON.
No dense 4096 by 4096 projector or star matrix is materialized; arithmetic cost depends on the finite exact Pauli-word support products generated.
claims.falsifier: Any failure of the exact Clifford anticommutators, Casimir centrality, block-dimension and swap trace counts, ordinary/swap trace identities, a negative characteristic coefficient in a Hermitian gap block, or a direct exact discrepancy in any block/ray certificate.
claims.novelty_boundary: The Spin(9) representation facts and Casimir method are standard. The audit is an independent internal verification of the star component, not a priority claim or a theorem for noncovariant channels, other representations, or arbitrary-dimensional broadcasting.
